Applied.Outcome: Resolved with no reply: all eleven recommendations taken. Written into the plan under "Decided before the build".

Replies.Text:
Design, Step 2: The Threads in the Editor. Eleven decisions, each with my recommendation first. Resolve with no reply to take them all; reply with the numbers you want otherwise, and I apply the result under "Decided before the build".

1. A selection to an anchor. AnchorMap gains PlainRange( Map, From, To ), the plain characters inside a source span as { Start, End } (null when the span holds none), the reverse of SourceRange; and the making of { Text, Prefix, Suffix } from a plain range, which Render.SelectionAnchor does for the rendered DOM, moves into Render.AnchorOf( Plain, Start, End ) (the trim and the context as today), so both views build the same anchor. PlainRange is tested in node with the map's fixtures.

2. The buttons. A selection-buttons component (bindings: anchor, text, at) holding Copy, Comment or Re-anchor here, and Start a new Subplan, with the actions that html-view has today moved into it; html-view and edit-view compute the anchor, the text and the position and show it. One markup, one behaviour; the ids (#copy-button, #comment-button, #subplan-button) stay on the Read view's. Alternative: a second copy of the buttons in edit-view; two copies drift.

3. When the editor offers them. On a non-empty main selection, once the mouse is up or a keyboard selection rests; placed under the selection's end (coordsAtPos); hidden on any edit or a collapsed selection. Copy always, copying the text as it reads (the plain text from the map; Ctrl+C in the editor copies the source, marks and all). Comment and Start a new Subplan only while the text is the saved one (not dirty, not stale), as the edit preview did; in Source mode too.

4. The scroll to a passage. A thread-selected that did not come from a mousedown in the editor (the thread header's anchor words, a card, a search hit) scrolls the editor to the thread's mark, centred (EditorView.scrollIntoView), and flashes it. The flash: a flash effect on the anchor field adding a class to the mark for a second, the keyframes in edit-view.css. The Read view keeps its scroll.

5. The pending. html-view's main one settles State.Pending only when Read is the view shown; edit-view settles it when Edit is: Select selects, scrolls and flashes; Scroll { text } finds the text in the map's plain, scrolls to it and flashes a temporary mark; Compose starts a comment on the whole document.

6. Re-anchor. The hint moves from the read section into document-editor, above whichever view is shown; Re-anchor here among the editor's buttons posts the anchor as the Read view does and selects the thread.

7. New Comment and Ctrl+Shift+C are offered in the CodeMirror Edit view too (the button's ng-show and the key's When become "a plan open, not archived").

8. A click off a mark in the editor does not deselect the thread: a click there places the cursor. Escape deselects, as it does now.

9. A document (the Readme, the instructions): no marks, Copy alone, in both views.

10. Tests. Node: PlainRange against SourceRange over the fixtures, both ways. Browser, CodeMirror mode: a selection in the editor shows the three buttons; Comment opens the compose card with the anchor's words; Start a new Subplan opens the subplan form; Re-anchor here moves a thread; the header's anchor words scroll the editor until the mark's box is inside the scroller, and the flash class comes and goes; a waiting item's link flashes the passage; a dirty text offers Copy alone. The smoke: the buttons on a selection in the editor.

11. Out of this step: the Read view's removal in CodeMirror mode (Step 3).

Applied.Outcome: The build was accepted as reported; no text change. Committed as "Markdown Editor: Step 2".

Replies.Text:
Build log, Step 2: The Threads in the Editor. Built as decided, with the notes below; in CodeMirror mode the editor now does what the Read view does with the threads. Resolve to have it committed as "Markdown Editor: Step 2"; reply where something should be otherwise.

What was done

1. The anchor map (decision 1): PlainRange( Map, From, To ) gives the plain range of the characters whose spans lie inside a source span, the reverse of SourceRange, by a binary search over the starts; Render.AnchorOf( Plain, Start, End ) is the making of { Text, Prefix, Suffix } that SelectionAnchor did inline, now called by both views. Tested in node against SourceRange and over the map's cases.
2. selection-buttons (2): a component (public/components/selection-buttons) with the three buttons and their actions moved out of html-view: Copy (the text as it reads), Comment or Re-anchor here (the POST to /anchor, then the reload and the select), Start a new Subplan; bindings anchor, text, at, main and done. html-view and edit-view compute the anchor, the text and the place and hand them over; the Read view's keeps the ids. The buttons' styles moved from html-view.css into the component's stylesheet; the host stays the positioned frame.
3. The editor's offer (3): Mirror calls Handlers.OnSelection on every selection change; edit-view waits 250 ms for it to rest, then maps the main range through PlainRange and AnchorOf, places the buttons under the selection's end with coordsAtPos, and offers Copy always and Comment and Start a new Subplan while the text is the saved one, on a plan that is not archived; a document gets Copy alone. An edit, a collapsed selection or a scroll of the editor takes them away; a button collapses the selection to its end when done. The map of the current text is kept while the text is the same.
4. The scroll and the flash (4): a thread-selected that did not come from a mousedown on a mark scrolls the editor to the thread's mark, centred (EditorView.scrollIntoView), and flashes it: a set_flash effect on the anchor field puts a flash-mark decoration over the range for 1.2 seconds, the keyframes (an accent ring fading) in edit-view.css. The anchor field builds its set with Decoration.set now, the flash a mark beside the anchors, and threads_at and anchors_of skip it.
5. The pending (5): html-view's main one leaves State.Pending alone while the CodeMirror editor is the view shown; edit-view settles it on open and on plan-loaded: Select selects (the card scrolled into view, the passage flashed through the selection), Scroll finds the words in the map's plain text as Render.ScrollToText finds them in the rendered text, Compose starts a comment on the whole document.
6. Re-anchor (6): the hint moved out of the read section into document-editor, above whichever view is shown, with its own width rule; State.StartReanchor and State.StartCompose no longer switch to Read while the CodeMirror editor is shown, so a comment or a re-anchor started from the editor stays in it.
7. New Comment and Ctrl+Shift+C (7) are offered in the CodeMirror Edit view: the header's button through EditorShown(), the key's act and its When ("a plan's Read view, or its CodeMirror editor").
8. No deselect on a click off a mark in the editor (8); a document gets no marks and Copy alone (9).
9. Tests (10): AnchorMap.test.js gained the PlainRange test; Ui.test.js a test that drives it all in CodeMirror mode: New Comment there; the closing thread's card scrolling the editor to its passage, in view and flashed; a mouse drag along a line offering the three buttons, Comment starting a compose on the words with the view staying Edit; re-anchoring with the hint above the editor, the button reading Re-anchor here and the thread moving; a pending select settled in the editor with the flash; Start a new Subplan opening the form; a dirty text offering Copy alone, the three back after undo. node --test: 194 pass (192 before: one node test and one browser test added), the whole suite run twice to the end after the fixes below. The smoke gained a check: a drag along a line offers the three buttons; the whole smoke (page and desktop) ends SMOKE OK with 40 checks.

Notes and departures

- The editor renders only the lines in view and around them, so a passage far down a long text has no mark in the DOM until the editor scrolls there; the browser test and its drag helper go through EditorView.findFromDOM to scroll the view to a line first. The scroll and the flash themselves were checked by a probe on a forty-paragraph text: scrollTop from 0 to 1808, the mark centred, the flash on and off.
- The buttons sit in the editor's box, not in its scroller, so a scroll would leave them behind the text: they are hidden on scroll instead. The test clicks them without scrolling them into view for that reason.
- A pending settled in the editor ends with a digest, since the load that brings it comes outside one; without it the card's selected class waited for the next digest.
- The flash is 1.2 seconds, the Read view's 1.6: the ring reads faster than a background fade.
- The buttons live beside the engine's host, not inside it: the Monaco wrapper empties its element when it opens, and the first smoke run found the buttons gone after Monaco had been in the box. The edit view's #editor is now a host inside a .editor frame that holds the buttons.
- Two fixes to the smoke itself: its drag goes through the view as the test's does, and the desktop part waits for the Hotkeys popup to take the focus before pressing Escape; that Escape raced the popup's focus and had failed once in Step 1's first run and once here, both times with nothing of these steps involved.
- Under the whole suite (every test file at once, several browsers) the test's drag ended a character short once; its expectations on the selected words are by containment now, not by the exact string.
- Nothing of the Read view changed for Monaco mode; the server tests ran untouched.
